target.title: fix: avoid false restart failure during startup migrations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators updating or restarting OpenClaw could receive a readiness failure after about 60 seconds even though the gateway was still healthy and completing a legitimate startup migration. Observed migrations can take substantially longer, causing the update path to report failure while the gateway becomes ready shortly afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed restart readiness owner now recognizes the canonical startup-migration lease and grants a bounded migration-aware wait, followed by the existing readiness window once migration work finishes. Normal startup failures still fail promptly, and non-migration restarts retain the existing timeout. The update subprocess also receives the update step's configured timeout so its outer watchdog cannot terminate a valid extended wait early.

## User Impact

Updates and managed restarts no longer report a false failure while a healthy startup migration is actively progressing. Crashes, stopped processes, stale leases, plugin/channel/version mismatches, and ordinary readiness timeouts retain their existing failure behavior.

## Evidence

- Added focused coverage for a healthy long migration and genuine readiness failures/timeouts.
- Focused Vitest proof: 334 tests passed across daemon service merging, the startup migration checkpoint, restart-health, daemon lifecycle, update command, and full update CLI suites.
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint checks passed; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Fresh autoreview after CI/review fixes reported no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.89).
- Blacksmith Testbox and AWS Crabbox were unavailable in this environment because the required organization/cloud credentials were not present; CI remains the remote Linux proof.

AI-assisted: implementation and validation were completed with Codex; the author reviewed the resulting code and behavior.

Implemented and committed the migration-aware restart fix.

Root cause:

- Managed restart health had a fixed 60-second deadline.
- Startup migrations run before the gateway listener becomes ready and can legitimately exceed that window.
- Package updates also wrapped `gateway restart` in a competing 60-second process timeout.

Fix:

- Uses the canonical startup-migration lease as the progress signal.
- Extends waiting only while the supervisor reports the process running.
- Caps migration waiting to one five-minute lease TTL, followed by a normal readiness window.
- Preserves prompt failure for crashes, stopped services, plugin/channel errors, stale PIDs, version mismatches, and ordinary non-migration timeouts.
- Propagates the configured update-step timeout to the restart subprocess.
- Reports the actual extended timeout duration.
- Covers both managed `gateway restart` and update verification; unmanaged in-process restarts remain listener-based.

Changed: `src/cli/daemon-cli/{restart-health,lifecycle}*`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts`, and `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint*`.
